answer: Arrival-Order Seed Crediting. New agents earn trust only from arrival slots near a bucket's nadir, when genuine traffic is thinnest. Each slot's credit is stored in a vault keyed to that bucket, so backdated registrations earn nothing. An attacker must flood many sable buckets with fresh identities and wait through each quiet window, paying wall-clock time and per-identity slot costs that scale with buckets occupied rather than with one bulk purchase.
